# CLI Options structs

## Purpose

A `mustard` subcommand keeps its flags in a small `pub struct <Command>Options` declared in the same module as the command function it configures. This keeps `clap` out of the command modules entirely: `apps/cli/src/cli.rs` owns the derive (the `Commands` enum with its `#[arg(...)]` attributes), and its `dispatch` builds the plain options struct by field shorthand before calling into the command. The payoff is that `init`, `config` and `add` stay callable as library functions — the Tauri backend and the in-file unit tests construct the options directly, with no `argv` in sight. The struct is data only: no methods, no validation, no default logic beyond the derived `Default`. Persisted configuration is not its job — `mustard_core::ProjectConfig` owns `mustard.json`, while `*Options` describes one invocation.

## Convention

Folder: apps/cli/src/commands/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 4

- File name is the subcommand in snake_case (`init.rs`, `config.rs`, `add.rs`, `install_nerd_font.rs` for `install-nerd-font`); the struct is the subcommand in PascalCase plus the `Options` suffix.
- All four members carry `#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]` and are introduced by the same one-line doc comment, `/// Flags accepted by mustard <subcommand>.`
- The struct sits immediately after the `use` block — the first item a reader meets past the `//!` module header, ahead of the module's private types and helpers.
- Fields are `pub`, one `///` line each saying what the flag does. Boolean flags are bare `bool` (`force`, `yes`, `dry_run`); a flag carrying a value is `Option<T>` (`InstallNerdFontOptions::font: Option<String>`).
- Field names mirror clap's long flag in snake_case, so the dispatch arm stays a shorthand literal: `dry_run` for `#[arg(long = "dry-run")]`, `yes` for `#[arg(short = 'y', long)]`.
- The command entry point takes the options **borrowed and last**: `pub fn init(project_path: &Path, options: &InitOptions) -> Result<()>`. A positional argument stays its own parameter — `add(cwd, template_spec: &str, options: &AddOptions)` — instead of becoming a field.
- The struct is read, never mutated: the three exemplars read in full turn a flag into intent at the call site (`git_flow::configure(project_path, !options.yes)`) rather than storing derived state on the struct.
- Tests live in the same file under `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` and lean on the derived `Default` — `&AddOptions::default()`, `&InitOptions { yes: true, ..InitOptions::default() }` — which is why `Default` is in the derive set even for a one-field struct.
- No `clap` attribute, no `serde` derive and no `impl` block on the options structs in the three exemplars read in full.

## How to apply

A new subcommand `foo` gets `apps/cli/src/commands/foo.rs`, registered by a `pub mod foo;` line in `apps/cli/src/commands/mod.rs` (the list is alphabetical). Inside the file: `//!` module header explaining what the command does and why, the `use` block, then the one-line doc comment over `#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)] pub struct FooOptions { … }`, then `pub fn foo(cwd: &Path, options: &FooOptions) -> Result<()>` with `anyhow::Result`. Add the matching variant to the `Commands` enum in `apps/cli/src/cli.rs`, carrying the `#[arg(...)]` attributes and the user-facing help text, plus a `dispatch` arm that builds `&FooOptions { … }` by shorthand — keep the names identical on both sides so no mapping code is needed. Do not add a field for something that is not a flag, do not derive `clap::Args` on the options struct, and keep `unwrap`/`expect` inside `#[cfg(test)]` only. When a flag selects a destructive path, follow `init`: the flag picks the branch, and the safety (backup, skip-existing, dry-run early return) is enforced in the command body, not encoded in the struct. One sibling in this folder departs from the suffix — `install_grammars::run` takes an owned `InstallGrammarsArgs` (visible in the `dispatch` arm of `apps/cli/src/cli.rs`); prefer `*Options` plus a borrow for a new flag-bearing subcommand.

## Examples

- Ref: apps/cli/src/commands/init.rs — the three-flag case (`force`, `yes`, `dry_run`), threaded unchanged through both `init` and `init_with_templates`; its tests build it with `..InitOptions::default()`.
- Ref: apps/cli/src/commands/add.rs — a single-flag struct beside a separate positional `template_spec: &str`; `options.force` is handed down to the copy routine as a plain `bool`.
- Ref: apps/cli/src/commands/config.rs — the minimal case: one `yes` field, converted at the call site into `!options.yes` for the shared `git_flow::configure`.
